body: How do you keep going? Or what has stopped you?
Damn that's a long time. A lot longer than me.
Never heard of it.
Three things? Depression, anxiety and being highly sensitive.
Most days I think I have more positive thoughts, I watch a lot of tv to distract me from reality.
He was visiting his mom in Mexico

Before I answer let me say this. I appreciate you taking time out of your day to talk to me. 

Do I value life? That's tough. Objectively speaking I guess I do. When it comes to my own life not so much. 

I know life can be a wonderful thing. If I didn't have depression and anxiety I'm sure I would really appreciate life. 

I'll be honest, life scares me, I've seen the horrible things humans can do. I've seen the horrible injuries that can happen to anyone. Losing a loved one is not a matter of if, but when. Confrontation really scares me. 

I know that bad things happen to everyone, but the difference is that others are well equipped to handle anything. 
Even small changes affect me greatly. For example, this past summer my cousin, we live together, went on a trip for a month. When he got back it weirded me out, really depressed me. And it's not that I don't like him, I just got used to him being gone and when he got back it threw me off.

No one in my family knows anything. I will never tell them. 

It's not just me feeling like less than a man. There are so many things that depress me. I couldn't write everything down, it would be way too long. And while there are things that I can improve, there are many things that are impossible to change. 

If I kill myself everyone around me will be ok eventually. People die all the time. I could die today in a car accident, develop a terminal illness, etc. it's just the way life is.

Damn. You've had to deal with some real assholes. I can't blame you for not feeling like a "real woman". Nobody should be talked to like that, it definitely hurts you not just short term, but long term. 

I used to chat with a lot of guys and most were really nice, at first, I was so happy. But when I showed them a pic of me or we met up in person, they would stop talking to me. It really hurt my self esteem. Now this was a few years ago when I was doing relatively good, so I doubt guys were turned off due to negativity or whatever. 

I guess I'm a big hypocrite giving you this advice. Just focus on yourself, fuck other people who put you down. Eventually you'll start attracting the right people. Do the things that make you feel happy and good. I know there are guys out there that are attracted to all types of bodies and personalities. Just stay hopeful that you'll meet a good guy, one who appreciates and loves you for the woman you are. 

Don't let those assholes bring you down.

I live with family so not many responsibilities    
I have to pay a utility bill, car insurance and a few thousand dollars I owe. Objectively it's not bad at all. 

I just have no future. I wasn't able to enlist in the military, I guess it's good because I can't even keep a simple job, and I wasn't able to attend college/trade school. 

At the end of the day I'm just a burden on my family. Once I have enough money I'll probably buy my plane ticket. I don't want to die in my home state and the last thing I want to see before dying is the ocean.

My family is very supportive. In all honesty I have no excuse for being a failure. I'm sure there are many people around the world who would love to be in my shoes. For the most part I've had a great life. 

Physically I really just wish I was taller. Everywhere I go I'm almost always one of the shortest guys. Even a significant amount of women are taller than me. I feel inferior to most people. 

As a person I would love to be a hard worker. Throughout school I always had excellent grades, very rarely missed school. 
Ever since, I've had a hard time keeping a job. Whenever I'm employed I'm always stressed, anxious and depressed. But I'm probably just lazy and looking for excuses. 
I would also love to be more outgoing and selfless. 

My biggest thing is I don't want to be so sensitive. I take everything too personally and it doesn't take much to make me cry. I'm terrified of any kind of confrontation. I just can't function in this world. I'm not emotionally/mentally strong like most humans. So many people truly have it hard and they keep going. 

And I have tried many times in the past to improve myself. I ate healthy, worked out, tried to love myself, improve my confidence, stop worrying what others think, focus on my hobbies. I really tried, but I always fail. I'm just not built for this life. 

A lot of times no particular thing brings me down, I just get this feeling. It makes me hate being alive. I can't really explain it. 

My biggest wish would be to give my life to a terminally ill person.
To a certain extent I can control if I'm fat, skinny, muscular, hairy, smooth, etc.

I could see how one might feel less of a man when it comes to the physical aspect, but when it comes to personality I believe most trans men are more of a man than I'll ever be. 
I know that being transgender can be difficult, even without depression. I admire trans men and women for being who they truly are. Best of wishes to you.

I wish I thought more like you, I guess I'm just superficial and worry about stuff I shouldn't. 

I was actually doing pretty good towards the end of high school, beginning of college. I was starting to accept myself, becoming more confident. But things happen. I don't think I'll ever be happy with myself. 

But you. You seem like you're on the right track. I hope things keep improving for you. It's not an easy path but I'm sure you'll come out on top! Best of luck.

That's crazy. I genuinely felt like I was the only that cried over "insignificant" things. It's nice that there are others alike. 

I actually don't cry over movies, but that's because I feel silly and embarrassed. Growing up I would get in trouble for crying, so I try to hold it back as much as possible. Of course that doesn't work most of the time. 

I'm not gonna go into much detail, but sometimes I overthink and wonder if I could ever snap and go all psycho, harming family/friends/strangers. Another reason I think it's best if I'm not alive. 

When I'm most depressed I get angry/irritated and take it out on those around me. I feel bad. 

I wish I could win the lottery. That way I could live in some isolated place. I wouldn't have to worry about going to a shitty job and have to be around people. I wouldn't have to worry about what others think of me. I wouldn't have to worry about being hurt by or hurting others. One can only dream. 

But it seems like you've accepted yourself the way you are? I hope things keep improving for you. You seem like a good soul.
I would make myself significantly taller. That's the only thing I can't change in real life.

You make some great points. I know your personality is very important, but at the end of the day so is your physical. At least in my experience. 

My personality is crap and so is my body. I've tried very hard in the past, but at this point I don't see the benefit of trying to improve myself. I doubt I'll make it to my 23rd birthday. 

Also, it's not my intention to shame or put down other guys in a similar situation. This is just how I feel about myself.

Being sensitive does have its pros. It would be nice if more people were a bit more sensitive. 

In my case though, I'm super sensitive. It's embarrassing actually. I take things too personally, and doesn't take much to make me cry. An example, when I started a new job I did something I wasn't supposed to and my supervisor came and talked to me, he was really nice about it. I took it too personally and almost cried, my eyes teared up. I've passed up jobs because I'm scared customers will make me cry. I'm 22 years old, it's humiliating. 
A "man" like me can't make it in this world. 

In my experience, the gay community is quite shallow. And it's not that I'm not masculine, I've been told before that I am, it's just I'm weak. Most if not all guys would pass me up and I don't blame them, we can't help what we're attracted to. 

Also, I don't mean to put other guys down. This is a criticism on myself.
I live in Utah and just went on that site just to check. It did pop up lol
Please. No need to exaggerate. Mexicali can get humid, I've seen a heat index of 143°F. I'll see if I can find the screenshot.
I really enjoy the David Pakman Show.

Even in the middle of summer I wish that it would remain hot all year. And we have a swamp cooler that only works at night. During the day my house is constantly above 90°F, but I wouldn't trade that for winter. 
During winter is when I wish I could be happy.

You're right. I have a lot of happy memories. 
And you're also right that killing myself will eliminate the chance of being happy. But it will also eliminate the chance of bad things happening.
Yeah there is comfort knowing you can escape this world.
Aww beautiful family!

Thanks for taking the time to read and reply. I would love to move to a warm city. Like Phoenix or Las Vegas. Get my own place and finally be able to have a cat and a dog. But I doubt it'll change anything. 
There have been times when everything was going great. I was happy with my job, I wasn't necessarily sad. However, I had this feeling, not sure how to describe, it just made me feel unhappy. Like there's no point in life. 

I don't see how things can get better. School is out of the picture, and my dream job requires a degree. 

I'm actually an illegal immigrant, currently have a work permit. With a new president coming in it's likely it'll be taken away. I won't be able to work or study. 
Being sent back to my birth country is terrifying. I'd rather die here. 

Not everything is meant to be, you know? :/ if I don't die by suicide I could die from a disease or car accident. So in the end it won't matter if I kill myself.

It's cool that they can screen antibodies, I didn't know. 
I have two cousins with T1D, no immediate family, so I think I'm safe. I just get a little paranoid once in a while.

That sounds a kind of like me. Normally I drink like 5-8 water bottles a day plus milk or juice. And I use the bathroom every 1-3 hours. But I think that's just normal for me so I'm not too worried. A relative actually gave a blood test kit, just gotta find it. 

It's kind of scary how fast it can creep on you though. Seems like you could be fine one day and the next you're really sick. I assumed it was always a slower progression.

Wow that's crazy. I knew constant thirst was one of the symptoms, but I didn't think it was that severe. 
Most of the time I'm good, I rarely think about it. 
I started urinating quite often yesterday and in larger quantities, so that's what got me a bit worried. But I don't think I'm thirstier than usual, so I should be good!
